page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Esv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for matrix mathematics. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1975.0 and a strong text processing score of 2658.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 7972.24 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7558.0. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate a high read-only small-block cached speed of 626.49 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write speeds drop to 42.29 GB/sec and 28.08 GB/sec respectively, contributing to a lower Passmark memory score in the bottom 25% tier. For specialized workloads, the hardware achieves a strong text generation speed of 302.13 tokens/sec on a small 135M LLM, but performance drops significantly on larger models, yielding a weak 8.06 tokens/sec on a 7B model.

The E16-8s_v6 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high memory capacity but lower compute requirements. By constraining the active vCPU count to 8 while retaining 128.0 GB of RAM, it helps reduce software licensing costs that are billed on a per-core basis. This resource profile is appropriate for memory-intensive applications such as relational databases, caching layers, enterprise applications, and light data processing tasks that do not require local ephemeral storage.
